Figure 4. Recorded 12-lead ECG examples across age-transfer settings. All panels show measured signals, not generated waveforms. A, A conduction-positive young-adult ECG detected by the unchanged older-adult model in the independent external cohort. B, A conduction-positive child detected by older-adult fine-tuning but missed by the model trained from scratch. C, A conduction-positive infant missed by older-adult fine-tuning; the scratch model also misses this case. Case selection is deterministic and outcome-conditioned: A is the lexicographically first record ID among young-adult true positives; B is the lexicographically first patient ID among child positives detected by fine-tuning but missed by scratch; C is the lexicographically first patient ID among infant positives missed by fine-tuning. No selection on waveform appearance was performed. All twelve standard leads show the first 10 seconds of the stored 100 Hz, physically scaled recordings. Each lead is centered by its ten-second mean; no additional filtering, smoothing, clipping, time warping or per-lead amplitude normalization is applied. All panels share the same voltage scale and identical lead-baseline positions. Every adjacent lead baseline is separated by the same 5.5 mV display offset in all three panels. This uniform spacing includes at least 0.55 mV clearance between adjacent traces at every recorded time point. Original waveform amplitudes in mV are preserved. Minor grid intervals are 0.04 s horizontally and 0.1 mV vertically; major intervals are 0.2 s and 0.5 mV. The calibration pulse is 1 mV high. Physical paper speed and millimeters per millivolt depend on reproduction size; use the plotted time axis and voltage calibration. Young-adult scores are the frozen ensemble probabilities with the original source threshold. Pediatric scores and thresholds are the saved calibrated out-of-fold probabilities and validation-selected age-band thresholds from the fold that held out each patient. TP and FN are defined against the computational harmonized conduction label, pending clinician review. The displayed pediatric probabilities and thresholds are model- and fold-specific and should not be compared as universal confidence measures. These selected examples illustrate model decisions and residual errors; they do not establish cohort-level accuracy, a learned mechanism, or clinical readiness. Figure 3 provides the cohort-level evidence; the pediatric experiment remains exploratory cross-validation on previously examined data.
